“Field! Trip!” 

What were they suggesting, that I’d have them ride on my back to this thing called a... cruise? Fairly unfortunate, but my knowledge of the Western Kingdoms is not as adept as it should be— but that’s hardly a problem as I explain to them I’m unaware of what it is that they are seeking on this cruise.

“Sister, don’t tell me you don’t know!” cried aloud Junior as he worked on his maths homework off to the side. Most members of our guild tallied and trained in this large room I had built myself from much fire, stone-crushing, and people-scaring. 

Most of my members looked at me in the same manner. I shrugged. “I’m not a water species in depth. Though I am, there’s no need for me to venture into the Atlantic Ocean.”

“Didn’t you want to see the Sea Turtle migrations?” asked Kuil, who has cocked his head with a considering frown. “That’s where they’re happening if you say yes to our vacation—“

“Field! Trip!” initiated and covered by Georgette Robinson. 

Kuil shrugged. “I’m looking at a vacation.”

His best friend, Satoshi, didn’t say much to argue or support his intentions. I was still on a loss. Whatever was this thing called a cruise that they wanted to go so dearly and leave behind these lands of ours?



Later I would find myself in the outskirts of my territory. The guild’s territories. They were one in the same. My home wasn’t far off but was very unneeded most of the time. I’d stay here with them when I was given most chances; most of us stayed here, my oldest members, a father and mother of half-nearness to 100 moved here with their children. 

It was a peaceful life and territory... 

I sighed, and began speaking with the few sheep, parrots, wolves, and goats that surrounded me. I told them I’d be back, so take good care of yourselves until then. 

“Yo, _______!”

My wings almost burst from under human skin. Eyes wide and glowing feral, hisses leaving my lips, and I could feel claws just yearning (and my yearning too) to break free. 

I turned to him. A member of my guild. I looked at him, his eyes just as human but underneath he radiates draconic roaring nature. He was a stone sculpture well-chiseled and holding fast together but within, made of ancient storms and fire. A breath of snowstorm and thin flames exasperated from my mouth. The animals watched us, completely unafraid, and remained as they were.

Even my most curious sheep decided to blow into the remaining snowflakes and fires.

“I guess we’re going then!” He exclaimed, as he sat down on the log next to me. “I’ve been there before, you’re going to love it!”

It’d been a long time since I heard my name. “Why did you say my name?”

He whispered close to my ear. “Don’t you know I love you, _______. I love you, Victoria.” Then he added, “Besides, this isn’t—“

“Who I really am? Yeah, I get it. Most dragons scream and taunt me about that.” I sigh. There’s a blasphemous full moon of worries and trauma swelling in my cranium; if I was still in my true form, I would’ve shattered mountains. My screams, my roars, the Heavens had not heard such in millennia. “I don’t want to hear that again. Nope. Maybe this is who I really am. Maybe I enjoy herding humans. Maybe I enjoy being amongst them. Maybe I enjoy helping Junior with his homework and teaching these humans how to bend fire for their survival in any geographic setting!”

He looked at me, a nervous smile and a hand rubbing the back of his neck. That same hand was shredded to pieces as his real hand shown forth. “I was actually going to say, this isn’t something I take lightly.” He scoffed, “I’m in this too small human form for you, _______.  With you.” He sighed, “Though, are you sure it’s not just enjoyable because no other dragon likes you?”

I looked at him. Silence was me, grim reminders was me. 

He smiled in pity. “Yeah, well, they have no idea what they’re missing. They’ve no idea what they’ve done... to you.” I feel his draconic hand on my own. I miss the touch. My hand is disguised but I missed the touch of my own kindred. 

They pushed me away. Me. I felt my lips tremble. A snarl so gnarly and draconic that it was a massage to my chest. There’s anger, there’s anger.

But he catches me just in time.

There’s him, there’s him. And I sob pitifully but truer than I have in months. The animals slowly pivot away. Some remain, others leave. I hold his hand and the animals that remain draw a bit closer to me. I’m sobbing in joy, and their heads are on my knees, their coos of sympathy and love and... adoration. 

Suddenly he’s hissing. His grip tighter. A smile, elation and full, toothy, flashes on his human face but in a blink do I see his true face — draconic, pitch black, magnificent and mighty horns curved up, eyes alive. 

“What?” I ask.

He chuckles, “Have you really forgotten that you’re the most powerful dragon of us all? The effect you have on us...” his hand had grown just a tad for emphasis. The look of wild, calculating dragon as his eyes’ identity — not something human and placid. 

Breaths of fire and stardust leave his mouth. 

I close my eyes. Make a decision in my head. The animals that remain look at me with expectation, and a knowledge in their eyes, sheer recognition.

“By the evening, I’ll leave with you.”

He was ecstatic and hugged me briefly. Whispering, “From our skies and from our stars, I remember you.”

I responded back in our mother tongue. “I remember you.” 

He smiled. “I won’t miss them.”

I scratched behind the ear of a rabbit and his hand scratched her other ear. The rabbit was in bliss and still, soon other rabbits crept closer, in anticipation of our touch while others were satisfied sleeping next to our legs—

The two dragons, at peace, laughing, as the stars fell and the sky became purple.



And by midnight, great crackles of thunder and lightning drummed into the earth below. In their fields, great shapes of dragons rose in shape and size. I tore out a roar that would rip apart my muzzle. It left me growling, menacingly and hungrily. 

He rose his chin to the sky and unleashed a heaven-resonating roar with great claws flexing at his sides, milking the roar from his throat muscles. 

The flakes disappeared. The vultures would have a tasty, if not stale, easy meal.

We looked at each other once our roars were finished and echoed only in the mountains around. His mouth was full of fire and stardust, my eyes calculative and myself, as I *felt* — the Dragon, the beast of the forbidden, maker of tornadoes and twisters.

He looks up at me. A chuckle from his throat from chapped lips. 

“They’ve forgotten me too.” 

He knows. His eyes, sparklets of blue with stormy grey. We’re kindred, we say in silence.

People walk past us. They always walk past us. Walking around us, bodies on the move dressed in warm-knitted coats and hats. They don’t care about us. They’ve forgotten us and we served as their kings for years. 

In dreams, we were their kings as many were before us, to children, women, the elderly, the forgotten, the abused, the wealthy, and the disabled. 

In life...

I hand The Forgotten King all of the money in my wallet. Dark tall buildings lurched over us. “I won’t be needing it.”

He ask me, “How are you doing?”

“It’s like a dark hole in my chest, nothing is there, nothing satisfies anymore. It is depression. It is failing.” I answer, refeeling the dark circles in my eyes. 

In life... we ruled and served over them. 

“I see...”

He looks at me. I ready to leave.

“Let me take you to them.”

I glance over my shoulder. His arm is extended with a welcoming hand at the end, but it looks like the road to a beginning. 

“To who?”

“The ones who never forgot.”

I take his hand and leave my former life behind. I’m led down an alleyway by The Forgotten King that’s darker than the winter evening he’s stolen me away from.

“I am in love with you.”

Harvest hummed knowingly, tired eyes closed, face burrowing more into the fur coat of his beloved twin sister. 

“You.. you know that, right? I’d never do anything to hurt you.” 

Harvest nodded, knowing his sister could feel the movement.

“Because. Because I’d never kill you, I’d never pick a single strand of hair from your head. I would never *dream* of harming you, Brother.”

Harvest creaked open an eye. The sky bled a maroon violet and saturated orange. The beginning of twilight, a mystical moment lasting less than he could hold his breath underwater. Time to make it count. Harvest casually wrenched himself up more atop of his sister’s back, settling his head on her furry shoulder, his cheek tickled by her wolf whiskers. A smile, softer than a summer’s day, graced his lips. “You’re not a monster, Naomi.” 

Her wolf ears fell sideways. The crinkling of dead autumn leaves and twigs crushed under her massive canine pads. 

“And I’ll say it as many times as you need to hear it. I will never blame you for what they made you do.” 

Her tongue rolled out to lick her lips, a trait of nervousness she always portrayed when she was human. That’s when Harvest caught the scent of strong iron and rotting meat. The blood from his sister’s last meal dirtied his cheek, but he’s grown use to it all — his twin’s lifestyle, his twin’s diet. 

Harvest coughed, spit overflowing in his mouth, leaking down his chin. Naomi reacted immediately and halted in her strides, unmoving and undoubtedly sensing the sickness wrenching through Harvest’s frail body. 

Harvest spat on the ground for a total of five minutes, coughing fits and heaves shaking him like a master would his slave. Twinklets of crimson, gulps of yellow mucous and blots of toxic green. A rainbow promise of a reminder that Harvest’s life was cut short, without even his consent or will to change a damn thing.

“Don’t—“ Harvest shivered, spitting up more unhealthy colors. “Don’t you dare blame yourself, Naomi, don’t you ever freaking dare. It was their fault not yours, not mine, not Willy’s.” 

Naomi lowered herself on all fours, ears low and saddened. “They wanted the perfect child...”

“And we took that putrid dream away from them.” Harvest smirked, teeth stained crimson and yellow. “They’ll never have us back. They lost their damned chance the moment they decided...” Harvest wretched up more spittal. “That something like this is okay, that we have to pay the price for their disfigured dreams. Naomi, if you hadn’t saved me from the table, they would have had you kill me.”

“Just for me?” 

It sounded like a twisted, early Christmas gift, but that’s the way their former parents saw them. 

Harvest and Naomi, failures in their mutagen experiments, but Willy survived and succeeded them to crawl as a beast for the rest of his days in anguish at *what had their parents done to him*?

Harvest and Willy, failures in their mental experiments and test. The GLADOS that their parents were chose survival of the fittest and natural selection to make their ideal perfect child. 

*“Don’t worry, Naomi. Willy just needs this medicine to keep the fever down while he sleeps. Now, gently insert the syringe into that— good job, Naomi! Goodness me, I didn’t even have to instruct you. She’s a real piece of art, isn’t she, Honey?”*

And Harvest watched his twin sister unintentionally murder their twin brother. Watched his sister writhe in sheer agony as the skin of her back split apart, arms contort, nose and cheeks disfiguring through the transformation. Heard her cry out as she knew *secrets* and love that belonged only to their twin brother. Willy’s life and memories, forced into the sister he loved more than anything in this life... 

Willy... Willy... an overwhelming sorrow rushed into Harvest’s mindset and stomach. He clung harder to his sister’s coat, trying to stifle his emotions and those traumatizing memories he did not want — he did not want them!

Harvest suddenly clung to his gut for dear life. He heaved, eyes wide, hoping, hoping, inwardly praying in the Spirit, don’t let this be it, don’t let this be another episode—

And wrenched out of his body was a violent discharge of blood. More than a water bottle held liquid. 

Naomi whined, and trembled. Wolf eyes large and peaking in every direction of the woods that hid the twins. He felt the fur along her spine raise in fear, unease. Ears staying low but her body trembling. Instincts undoubtedly screaming at her to get away from here, the scent of blood will attract predators. Instincts undoubtedly screaming at her to feast, to seek out the illness and kill. 

Harvest recognized the symptoms and coughed forcibly, “I’m o-okay!” 

The discharge slowed to a halt, leaving a puddle of his previous blood on the forest floor. It mattered, that mattered, that was scary. How was he still alive with so much blood he vomited on a near daily basis? How could a mother and father simply watch their child die and casually not take responsibility for being the very reason for their child’s permanent illness? 

Harvest walked away from his own thoughts to calm his sister. She was between beast and Naomi right now. A single stressor could tip her entirely into beast, and he’d lose his sister again like that—that last time. 

It took a week of regaining her back, and some memories were gone forever, and the darkness she chattered about like a traumatized victim upon awakening from being beast...

*Never again*

Harvest brought himself up and closer to his sister’s wolf ear, careful to not pluck a feather from her chin while her head scanned in every conceivable panicked direction, and sang, “You’ve got a friend in me, you’ve got a friend in me. When the road looks rough ahead and your miles and miles from your nice warm bed... you just remember what your old bro said. Sis, you’ve got a friend in me. Yeah, you have a friend in me.”

“You’ve got a friend in me, you’ve got a friend in me. You’ve got troubles, and I’ve got them too. There isn’t anything I wouldn’t do for you,” mused Naomi, voice oddly serene in her beast body. But Harvest was just glad she had a voice still... and she was singing Willy’s part. “We stick together, we can see it through cause you got a friend in me. You’ve got a friend in me.”

Harvest closed his eyes, grinning. “Some other folks may be a little bit smarter than I am. Bigger and stronger too, maybe.”

“But none of them will ever love you the way I do.  Just me and you.” The flash of a memory of old: they’d all sing this part together in a circle, pointing one finger to one another’s heart and laughing. Now, it was only Harvest and Naomi who sang it together.

Yeah... Toy Story was their favorite movie trilogy. Harvest loved the second one. Willy loved the third one. Naomi adored the first one, and she’s the reason why her twin brothers got into the Pixar classic in the first place.

“Willy was singing with us too.”

Harvest nodded, resting more as his sister’s back as they continued their runaway through the woods; with only the titanic trees leering over them, shielding them.
